texts.preamble: Kcg Oil & Food Pvt. Ltd. Thru. Abhay Gupta ... vs U.O.I. Thru. Secy. Health & Family ... on 2 November, 2020 Bench: Alok Singh, Karunesh Singh Pawar High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench ?Court No. - 3 Case :- Misc. Bench No. - 18694 of 2020 Petitioner :- Kcg Oil & Food Pvt. Ltd. Thru. Abhay Gupta & Anr. Respondent :- U.O.I. Thru. Secy. Health & Family Welfare,New Delhi & Ors. Counsel for Petitioner :- Anurag Narain,Shailendra Kumar Misra Counsel for Respondent :- A.S.G. Hon'ble Alok Singh,J. Hon'ble Karunesh Singh Pawar,J. Heard Sri Anuraj Narain, learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri S.B. Pandey, learned Assistant Solicitor General of India assisted by Sri Raj Kumar Singh, learned counsel for opposite parties and perused the record.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that respondent no.3 does not have any power or authority to issue impugned advisories which have an effect of amending Regulations which ought to have been framed under Section 92 of the Food Safety and Standards Act,2006 and the same is without any statutory force; the impugned advisory is neither covered under Section 92 and 93 of the FSS Act,2006 nor having been in consonance with section 16(2) and 18(2) (d) of the Act moreover in view of Section 5 and 6 of the Act of 2006 the respondent no.3 is not having any authority. Ltd. When the matter is taken up today learned counsel for the petitioner submits that statement has been given by learned counsel appearing for Union of India before Delhi High Court that notification dated 23.9.2020 has been withdrawn by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that respondent no.3 does not have any power or authority to issue impugned advisories which have an effect of amending Regulations which ought to have been framed under Section 92 of the Food Safety and Standards Act,2006 and the same is without any statutory force; the impugned advisory is neither covered under Section 92 and 93 of the FSS Act,2006 nor having been in consonance with section 16(2) and 18(2) (d) of the Act moreover in view of Section 5 and 6 of the Act of 2006 the respondent no.3 is not having any authority. When the matter is taken up today learned counsel for the petitioner submits that statement has been given by learned counsel appearing for Union of India before Delhi High Court that notification dated 23.9.2020 has been withdrawn by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India.
